description: Internal Goal Contract gallery — worked examples spanning the model (three axes, evidence types, governance, faithfulness). Generated by make_goal_gallery.py.

examples.name: Prove payment capture is idempotent (proof-first)
examples.summary: A full session: read the code, formalize, hit a COUNTEREXAMPLE, diagnose and fix it, re-verify to a PROOF, add regression tests, and get a non-doer sign-off. Step through the flow on the left. Ends met ∧ governed ∧ certified, with one honest residual (concurrency).

examples.name: Get tax-bracket edge cases right (decomposition-first)
examples.summary: The 'edge cases matter' loop: formalize, DECOMPOSE the input space into regions, cover them with tests, catch a boundary off-by-one, fix it, then PROVE monotonicity. Governed by 'generated tests must be decomposition-backed'. Ends met ∧ governed ∧ certified, with a rounding-mode assumption.

examples.name: All three axes green
examples.summary: settle is proved, its policy holds, and a non-doer certified the definition — met ∧ governed ∧ certified.

examples.name: Met but NOT governed
examples.summary: A VerificationResult exists (so the criterion is MET), but it is refuted and never re-proved — the policy fails, so the goal is NOT governed. The headline case: met ≠ done.

examples.name: Met + governed, NOT certified
examples.summary: Proved and policy-clean, but no non-doer has signed off on the definition of done — certified is still open. Green work, unreviewed bar.

examples.name: Certified but NOT met
examples.summary: A reviewer approved the definition and every clause is covered (certified), but no VerificationResult exists yet — the work is unfinished. The right target, in progress.

examples.name: Any artifact is evidence
examples.summary: Five criteria, five kinds of evidence — a proof, a decomposition, a generated test suite, a plain diff, and a documentation note. Evidence need not be formal; a policy decides if it's strong enough.

examples.name: A diff isn't enough on a high-stakes path
examples.summary: The criterion is met by a Diff, but settle is high-stakes and the policy demands a proof or a decomposition in lineage — so the goal is blocked (not governed). Rigor lives in the policy.

examples.name: Override: policy disabled (recorded)
examples.summary: The same high-stakes diff, but the goal explicitly DISABLES the policy — an on-the-record override, never silent. The goal is governed again, and the disabled rule is visible in the contract.

examples.name: Uncovered intent clause
examples.summary: The intent has two clauses but the acceptance covers only one — so even a proved, reviewed goal is NOT certified: the definition doesn't fully capture the intent.

examples.name: Self-review can't certify
examples.summary: The agent that authored the criteria is also the reviewer — a doer can't certify its own bar, so certified stays false. Certification needs a different principal.
